# Aims:

Integrate field investigations, remote sensing, and modeling to reveal cross-scale mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of robust models for understanding ecosystems — particularly forests — and improving forest management to enhance human well-being.


# Forest above ground biomass estimation

**How to estimate forest AGB across large spatial scale?**

![](photo/AGB_estimation.png){width="100%" style="border-radius: 6px; margin-bottom: 0.75rem;"}

LiDAR-based modeling of forest above-ground biomass (AGB) using USGS 3DEP and NEON airborne point clouds, integrated with GEDI spaceborne LiDAR footprints and ESA CCI Biomass products for cross-scale validation. Built a large-scale processing pipeline that derives canopy structure metrics (height percentiles, density, rumple index) and predicts plot-level AGB with Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and stacked ensemble models, evaluated with grouped cross-validation and SHAP-based interpretation.

**Tools:** R (lidR, lasR, terra, sf), Python (scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, SHAP)

# Ecosystem response to disturbances

**How do disturbances regulate ecosystem functioning?**

![](photo/climate_extremes_merged_ecosystem.png){width="100%" style="border-radius: 6px; margin-bottom: 0.75rem;"}

Climate extremes are projected to become more frequent and intense in the future, posing potentially severe yet poorly understood consequences for ecosystem functioning and carbon cycling.

**Publication:** Chu, D., Zhang, L., Wu, H., He, H., & Ren, X. (2026). Future climate extremes enhance interannual variability of net primary production in Central Asia. *Environmental Research Letters.* <https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ae6dd4>

**How do disturbances drive forest loss and its succession?**

![](photo/tree_mortality.jpg){width="100%" style="border-radius: 6px; margin-bottom: 0.75rem;"}

Quantifying forest loss trends and drivers across large spatial extents using time-series satellite imagery. The workflow integrates Hansen Global Forest Change data with climate and topographic covariates to attribute disturbance to fire, harvest, and insect outbreak.

**Tools:** R, Python, GEE

---

# Cooling effect of urban green space

**How does the urban green space regulate the temperature?**

![](photo/urban_green_space_cooling_effect.png){width="100%" style="border-radius: 6px; margin-bottom: 0.75rem;"}

Quantifying how the structure and composition of urban green spaces moderate land surface temperature across cities. Integrates USGS 3DEP airborne LiDAR-derived canopy metrics (height, cover, vertical complexity) with land cover and satellite-derived LST to model cooling magnitude as a function of canopy structure, patch geometry, and surrounding impervious context.

**Tools:** R (lidR, terra, sf, lme4), Python (xarray, rasterio, scikit-learn)
